description: Recorded real SURGEDAT peak storm-surge databases (Louisiana State University, Southern Regional Climate Center). Nothing is synthetic; each CSV is the served file byte-verbatim (classic Mac OS carriage-return line ends, Mac Roman text), stored gzip-compressed so line-ending and end-of-file hooks cannot rewrite it.
source: SURGEDAT, https://surge.climate.lsu.edu/data.html, offered on that page as freely available. Cite: Needham, H.F. and B.D. Keim, 2012: A Storm Surge Database for the U.S. Gulf Coast. International Journal of Climatology, 32(14), 2108-2123, doi:10.1002/joc.2425.
transport: surge.climate.lsu.edu serves its leaf certificate (CN=surge.climate.lsu.edu, issuer InCommon RSA Server CA 2) without the intermediate. The intermediate was taken from Mozilla's CCADB intermediate report (https://ccadb.my.salesforce-sites.com/mozilla/MozillaIntermediateCertsCSVReport; SHA-256 87E01CC4DD0C9D92A3DBD49092FF13F9CD387445CDC57E5B984E1B7721B5B029, issued by USERTrust RSA Certification Authority), the chain was verified with `openssl verify` against the system roots, and the files were fetched with full TLS verification using that intermediate.
notes: Used by tests/test_storm_surge_source.py. The database states most heights in both feet and metres; four pairs in the global file (one surge, three storm tide) disagree beyond their stated rounding, which the parser reports as conflicts, and none in the Gulf file do.
